answer: Paper mail is a slow relic, and that slowness is the point. Each identity earns rewards only after it returns a one-time code printed on a postcard sent to a distinct street address, rechecked with a fresh card every few months. Addresses are deduplicated, and known mail drops and PO boxes are refused. A real cabin by a jetty qualifies; a dune of a thousand fakes needs a thousand real doors, each rented and someone paid to collect the mail, and every renewal repeats that cost.
